To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
pigeons do not respond in spaced patterns unless they have a stimulus to peck, and that the pattern of collateral pecking that develops is non-arbitrary and species specific.
the pigeons in this experiment did not respond in the manner required by the spacing schedule, but did so when an alternative stimulus correlated with reinforcement was available.

the spacing performance of pigeons is mediated by collateral pecking on a non-contingent stimulus, and that the collateral behavior that occurs in the spacing procedure is non-arbitrary, species dependent, and is not determined by the contingencies of reinforcement in the procedure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of collateral behavior in the control of discrete-trial spacing performance in the pigeon.
the role of collateral behavior (behaviour that occurs concurrently with the behaviour of interest) in shaping performance in the pigeon.
the role that collateral behavior plays in mediating the performance of the pigeon on the discrete-trials spaced responding procedure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
spaced responding is a function of collateral behavior.
the spacing procedure is not a good procedure for studying spaced responding, at least in the case of pigeons.
, in general, the form that collateral behaviour takes may be non-arbitrary and species dependent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pigeons are not capable of spacing their responses to the same extent as rats.
the pigeon's ability to refrain from responding in the presence of a stimulus correlated with reinforcement depends on its ability to engage in other behavior in the presence of that stimulus.
the pigeon's response repertoire is not sufficiently broad to allow for the development of efficient spaced performance on the discrete-trial spacing schedule.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pigeons may fail to meet the response requirements for a schedule of spaced responding because they are not able to refrain from responding on that schedule.
the form of the collateral behavior is important for the success of spaced responding.
the spacing procedure is not as simple as it may appear to be.
